key_insight: This paper introduces LingBot-Video, a DiT-based video pretraining framework that uses Mixture-of-Experts to better align video generation with embodied intelligence needs. The core idea is to trade generic content-creation priorities for efficiency and physical realism more suitable for robot control.
problem_solved: Existing video generative models are optimized for visual fidelity and creative generation, which creates a domain mismatch for robotics and embodied intelligence. They are often too compute-heavy and not physically grounded enough to serve as effective pretraining for robot control.
method: Build a DiT-based video pretraining paradigm tailored specifically for embodied intelligence.
Replace dense architecture components with Mixture-of-Experts to improve scalability and computational efficiency.
Shift pretraining toward representations that better support physical understanding and downstream robot control.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a more scalable way to pretrain video models that transfer better to robotics tasks. It could reduce the gap between generic video generation and practical embodied agents.

paper_title: Scaling Mixture-of-Experts Video Pretraining for Embodied Intelligence
paper_authors: Shuailei Ma, Jiaqi Liao, Xinyang Wang, Jingjing Wang, Chaoran Feng
